evidence.field: File description, original image link, creation record, and license
evidence.text: The exact file page identifies the asset as 彡 in Shuowen seal-script style, cites Hanziyuan image s06481 as its source, records the Inkscape file upload in 2007, and states that the ancient-script representation is public domain. The supplied direct SVG URL matches the local asset; inspection of its SVG paths shows three curved strokes forming 彡. This is a modern redraw, not an artifact photograph.
evidence.title: File:彡-seal.svg — Wikimedia Commons

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry says 景 was used for shadow and sun-shadow, and describes 影 as 景 with 彡 added; it says 景 and 影 later specialized into separate written forms. It cites later lexicographic accounts attributing the addition to Ge Hong. This supports the reported graphic differentiation, but the attribution is not direct evidence of who first formed 影.
evidence.title: [A01275] 影 — Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.field: Rubbing of the Cuan Baozi Stele: transcription, date, and object description
evidence.text: The catalog transcribes 影命不長 and dates the stele to 405. It identifies the cataloged object as a rubbing and reports the stele was excavated in 1778; this is a dated attestation conveyed through the museum record, not direct inspection here of the original inscription.
evidence.title: 晉爨寶子碑墨拓本　軸 — National Palace Museum

evidence.field: File description, source attribution, original link, and license
evidence.text: The exact 景-seal.svg description page identifies 景 in Shuowen seal-script style, points to Hanziyuan image S04804, and states public-domain reuse for the ancient-script representation. Its original image link is available on that page. This is a modern vector redraw; it may illustrate the graph named in historical accounts as the base for adding 彡, but is not evidence for the date or shape of an early 影 compound.

search_audit.outcome: Opened and inspected the exact Commons 彡 file page, Taiwan MOE variant entry, and National Palace Museum stele-rubbing catalog. The official records support the image identity, reported graphic differentiation, and 405 transcription.

search_audit.query: Official Unihan character records U+5F71, U+666F, U+5F61
search_audit.outcome: Attempted all three character-specific Unicode records; the web tool returned access errors for each. Local exact reading rows remain separate from externally verified evidence.

search_audit.query: 景 seal script Wikimedia Commons exact file description page
search_audit.outcome: Opened and inspected the exact Commons page. It verifies a modern seal-style redraw of 景, its Hanziyuan source reference, direct original link, and public-domain statement.

gaps: The local SVG pixels and exact file description confirm the asset is 彡, not 景. The 影 formation account describes 景 with 彡 added, so this asset illustrates the semantic/graphic component but does not show a dated occurrence of the complete character.

No secure early-form sequence for complete 影 was established. The MOE dictionary reports 景-to-影 differentiation and later attribution of 彡's addition to Ge Hong, but this does not establish the original designer or original design.

The 405 occurrence is cataloged from a rubbing and supported by later scholarship; no contemporary original inscription was independently inspected. Earlier Han-end and lost-stele first-attestation claims remain disputed.

The Unicode GetUnihanData pages for 影, 景, and 彡 were inaccessible. Local exact kMandarin and Baxter–Sagart rows are supplied in the input but are not externally verified by this invocation. No new pronunciation claim is made.
No first dates for portrait, reflection, image, or photograph senses, or a complete semantic path from shadow to those senses, were established.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script style; modern vector redraw uploaded in 2007
items.tradition: Small seal-script style representation of 彡
items.caption: A modern seal-style redraw of 彡, the graphic-semantic element in the conventional account of 影. Historical accounts describe 影 as 景 with 彡 added to distinguish the shadow writing; this image shows 彡 alone.
items.alt: Three black, curved strokes sweep diagonally upward across a white square, forming 彡.
items.selection_reason: It correctly identifies the supplied asset and illustrates the component named in the reported 景-plus-彡 account. It is not an early artifact or an example of the complete character 影.
items.rights: The exact Commons description page states public-domain reuse for this ancient-script representation.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script style; modern vector redraw uploaded in 2014
items.tradition: Small seal-script style representation of 景
items.caption: A modern seal-style redraw of 景, the graph that historical accounts describe as used for shadow before 彡 was added in 影.
items.alt: A black seal-style graph for 景, with 日 above 京, centered on a white square.
items.selection_reason: Pairs the correctly identified 景 base with the 彡 component to help explain the reported graphic differentiation. Neither modern redraw documents an early compound form of 影.
items.rights: The exact Commons description page states public-domain reuse for this ancient-script representation.

limitations.text: Both selected glyphs are modern digital redrawings in Shuowen seal-script style. They illustrate the separately sourced graphs 景 and 彡 but do not document a dated ancient occurrence or the precise appearance of an early 影.
